video.title: How to Get People to Pay You (Free, No Audience)

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Caleb Panza, co-founder of Post for Me, a $10/month social-media posting API for developers launched after he and his co-founder Matt lost their jobs. With ~500 X followers, Caleb posted Stripe MRR milestones publicly, and built a support-driven content engine (human live chat, Linear, NotebookLM, AI articles) that got them recommended by Google and LLMs. They went from $500 MRR at five months to $5k at eight months and past $10k, but churn rose from 10% to over 17%, so they paused features to fix retention. He shares his tech stack and a playbook: solve your own problem, ship small, iterate daily.

tactics.name: Build in public with MRR milestone screenshots
steps: Screenshot Stripe at every $100 (later $500) MRR gained
Post on X with the days taken to reach it
Reply to every reply for the first week
Shift tone from apologetic to confident as numbers grow

quote.text: Like if, if they're journey helped me, why don't I just for fun, grab these screenshots for every $100 that we make in monthly recurring?
quote.speaker: Caleb Panza

tactics.name: Support-driven AI SEO content engine
steps: Run human-only live chat and respond fast
Log any problem raised by 2+ customers in Linear
Consolidate notes and support/Discord threads in NotebookLM
Generate a resource article with AI, lightly edit
Publish 1-3 per week with strong metadata so Google and LLMs pick it up

quote.text: We do things by hand, note how we do them by hand, and then apply the by hand notes to AI in order to automate it in the future.
quote.speaker: Caleb Panza

tactics.name: Pause roadmap to fix churn
steps: When churn rose from 10% to 17%, pause net-new features
Invest in telemetry/analytics to see where users get value or drop off
Use light Google Ads as an experiment to learn

tactics.name: SaaS launch playbook
steps: Pick a problem you personally felt
Brainstorm, chisel to smallest shippable step
Ship fast and iterate one small improvement daily based on usage
Use GitHub for code even if non-technical

tactics.name: Say yes to everything until you can afford not to
steps: Accept design, marketing, WordPress, Webflow jobs
Use agency income to fund product

quote.text: I like to say yes to everything until you can afford not to.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Churn can quietly rise even while MRR grows; MRR posts often ignore it.

quote.text: the more people started asking, yeah, but nobody's talking about churn

warnings.warning: Big spikes lead to big dips; prefer consistent growth.

quote.text: Big spikes equal big dips period
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Churn equilibrium: recurring revenue flattens when churn offsets new revenue; usually users fail to onboard in the first 10 minutes.

quote.text: In my experience, it's usually happening, you know, in the first 10 minutes that like they just don't fully onboard
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Don't keep code only locally or in Google Drive; use GitHub.

quote.text: stop storing code in Google Drive, or just like locally on your computer
quote.speaker: Caleb Panza

warnings.warning: Employment can be fragile: others' poor financial decisions can expose your family.
Transcript is Whisper tiny; product and tool names (Post for Me, Unkey, Claude) are reconstructed.

lessons.lesson: Transparency is rare and builds trust without a big audience.
One customer reporting a problem represents many silent ones; treat n=1 as signal.
Do it manually first, document, then automate with AI.
Structure content to be cited by LLMs (AI SEO) to earn inbound customers.

quote.text: we have gotten many customers coming to us since then saying chat GPT sent me
quote.speaker: Caleb Panza

lessons.lesson: Target an underserved segment (developers) of a crowded category (social posting).

quote.text: this app is pointed towards more technical people, developers, and that wasn't really being done
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Low entry pricing with unlimited usage-based upgrade paths grows revenue from scaling customers.
Rock bottom moments often push people to start.

quote.text: rock bottom can be a very powerful thing
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Fast human support early builds trust and surfaces content ideas.
Agency work can bridge years until a product launches.

quote.text: It took us two years of working on other people stuff.
quote.speaker: Caleb Panza
